title: When the Parish Wakes
premise: Coral Yarrow, a night dispatcher in the fading parish town of Marrow's End, receives two letters: one confessing to a fifteen-year-old drowning ruled accidental, and one promising a second death unless Coral delivers the letters to the police himself. As he digs into the old case, he discovers the killer is someone inside the investigation — using his own meticulously filed dispatch logs as a map. The final letter names Coral as heir to the victim's estate, revealing the murders are about inheritance and belonging; Coral must bait the killer with a forged confession of his own, surviving an ambush at the drowned quarry where it all began.
about_author: Gideon Eriksen is the pen name of a former small-town records clerk who spent a decade listening to police scanners before turning to fiction. He writes slow-burn mysteries about ordinary people who know too much.

chapters.title: The Night Shift Alphabet
chapters.summary: Coral Yarrow's POV. We meet him at 3 a.m., filing dispatch logs with obsessive precision, the only person in Marrow's End who knows every street and secret by heart. A quiet call from an address that shouldn't exist unsettles him. Beat: loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Two Envelopes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Twin letters arrive: one confessing to the 2009 drowning of Ada Quill, one promising 'the next name is yours.' No fingerprints, no return address. Coral hesitates over calling the police. Beat: dread blooming under routine.

chapters.title: Detective Voss
chapters.summary: Detective Imogen Voss's POV. She takes Coral's statement, dismissive until he recites case details from memory that were never made public. She begins to wonder whether the dispatcher is witness or suspect. Beat: wary alliance formed on unequal footing.

chapters.title: What the Logs Remember
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He pulls five years of dispatch records and finds calls from the same burner number logged the night Ada died — calls erased from official files but not from his backups. Someone inside cleaned the record. Beat: the thrill and terror of being right.

chapters.title: The Quill House
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She visits the decaying Quill estate, where Ada's brother Edmund guards the family's land deeds and a locked study. He mentions a will never probated. Beat: inherited rot, wealth as a wound.

chapters.title: Third Letter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A third letter arrives naming a date: Sunday, the parish festival. It praises Coral's filing system by name — the killer has been in his office. Beat: violation; home is no longer safe.

chapters.title: Parish Politics
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She interviews councilman Aldous Renner, whose development deal depends on the Quill land, and notices his alibi for 2009 was supplied by the then-sheriff. Beat: power revealed as a web of favors.

chapters.title: Ada's Friend
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. He tracks down Nell Barrow, Ada's childhood friend, now a hospice nurse, who says Ada was going to contest her family's will the week she drowned. Beat: grief given a shape and a motive.

chapters.title: Erased
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. The backup logs Coral kept vanish from the taxi office overnight; the office manager swears no one entered. Voss realizes the killer has access she can't trace. Beat: the ground shifting under the investigation.

chapters.title: The Fourth Letter
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The fourth letter accuses Coral himself: 'You were on shift that night too, weren't you? Five years ago you took the call and did nothing.' Coral can't remember — or won't. Beat: guilt as an unreliable narrator.

chapters.title: Old Dispatch Tapes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In a storage unit he finds analog tapes from 2009, including his own young voice logging a distress call from the quarry that was never dispatched. Beat: self-reckoning; complicity without malice.

chapters.title: Nell Disappears
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Nell Barrow misses her shift; her house shows signs of hurried departure, not abduction. Voss suspects Nell fled from the killer — or toward him. Beat: the clock starts audibly ticking.

chapters.title: Edmund's Study
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral breaks into the locked Quill study and finds the unprobated will: everything left not to Edmund but to 'the child who answers the night line' — a clause pointing at Coral. Beat: belonging weaponized; inheritance as a trap.

chapters.title: Voss Follows the Sheriff
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. She tails the retired sheriff to a marina meeting with Renner and Edmund. She photographs them passing an envelope and is spotted. Beat: hunter becoming hunted.

chapters.title: Fifteen Years of Sundays
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Reconstructing the tapes and letters, Coral maps the killer's pattern: each letter quotes dispatch phrasing only he uses. The killer learned language from listening to him — or is him, split off somehow. Beat: paranoia cresting.

chapters.title: The Confession Bait
chapters.summary: Voss and Coral, POV alternating. They draft a fake fifth letter 'confessing' Coral's guilt and stage its delivery through the taxi radio system, betting the killer monitors the frequency. Beat: desperate partnership, trust extended on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Festival Night
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. At the parish festival, the trap springs on the wrong man — Edmund, caught delivering yet another letter he claims he was forced to write. Realization: there are two hands in this. Beat: climax inverted; the net catches a puppet.

chapters.title: The Quarry
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. A final letter lures Coral alone to the quarry at night: 'Come claim your inheritance.' There he faces the true killer — the office manager, Ada's secret half-sibling, who has spent years inside Coral's world learning his files, his voice, his loneliness. Beat: confrontation; the killer's motive is belonging denied.

chapters.title: Waterline
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The killer forces Coral to reenact Ada's drowning call-for-call; Coral uses his encyclopedic knowledge of the quarry's dead zones to stall until Voss, tracking the staged radio traffic, arrives. The killer goes into the water himself. Beat: survival through the very obsession that endangered him.

chapters.title: Probate
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Arrests ripple outward: Renner, the retired sheriff, the cover-up laid bare. The will is read; Coral, legally Ada's named heir, must decide what to do with a fortune built on silence. Beat: justice partial, accounting begun.

chapters.title: What Coral Keeps
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral funds a memorial for Ada and quietly pays Nell's debts, keeping only enough to leave the taxi company. He burns nothing — instead donates his full archive to the county records. Beat: inheritance transformed into repair.

chapters.title: When the Parish Wakes
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, dawn. On his last morning shift, the phones stay quiet, and the town feels briefly legible and forgivable. A new dispatcher asks how he memorized it all. 'I listened,' he says. Beat: belonging finally earned, not inherited.
